prediction.likelyOutcome: U.S. Bank is a heavy favorite to obtain both the in rem foreclosure judgment and the in personam money judgment for the note balance at the bench trial, given the documented default, the forbearance agreement, and Penn Realty's failure to object to the combined pleading. The main uncertainty is not who wins but how much is ultimately collectible net of the foreclosure sale proceeds and the absence of any identified guarantor, and the case will likely resolve at or very near the pleaded $46,290,900.25 principal figure with additional but unquantified contractual interest, fees, and costs layered on top.

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court held Penn Realty breached the loan agreement and entered an in personam money judgment for U.S. Bank of $51,392,086.96 (no judgment in mortgage foreclosure was entered); the Third Circuit affirmed that judgment in a separate unpublished opinion (No. 23-2185, Sept. 25, 2024). In this precedential appeal the Third Circuit upheld the subsequent execution sale of the apartment building under Fed. R. Civ. P. 69(a) and affirmed the denial of the borrower's motion to quash.
